text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's consumer climate in January remains at the same level as in December, showing a significant change compared with the beginning of 1996 when January triggered a consumer slump which lasted for several months, a recent survey by the Demoskop polling institute said.
- The number of Polish-based firms exhibiting their products at the Zagrzeb international fair in Croatia grew by 300 percent in 1996 compared with the year before.
In the first ten months of 1996, trade between Croatia and Poland grew by 10 percent compared with the same period the year before.
- Poland's current account deficit in 1996 was at $8.3 billion, more than $2 billion less than preliminary estimates, the economy ministry said.

- The Polish State Railways (PKP) will change its employment stucture and increase the number of workers with higher education to 10 percent in a move to adapt the company to European standards, PKP said.
- Poland's furniture exports grew by 20 percent in 1996 compared with the year before, furniture makers said.
- Polish Development Bank (PBR) is planning a new share issue to provide PBR the funds needed to participate in the privatisation of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK).
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's computer hardware and software sales reached $1.9 billion in 1996, a market report by the Biuro Reklamy advertising firm said.
- Foreign investment in Poland in the last seven years reached $11 billion, with no individual investment less than $1 million, the finance ministry said.
- Airbus Industries plans to develop a new large passenger aicraft and expects that Poland's aviation industry could participate in its production, Airbus' deputy president Pierre Carpent said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's treasury ministry will call a public tender to choose a consulting firm to produce information documents for companies entering the CTO over-the-counter market.
The document project will be financed by the World Bank, the treasury ministry said.
- The listed Stalexport foreign trader's net profit in 1997 will grow by 60 percent, the company said.
Stalexport also plans a convertible bond issue later this year.
ZYCIE

- The Warsaw-branch of the U.S.-based Grey Advertising firm reported the highest profits of all Grey's branches in 1996 and brought 1.5 percent of the firm's total revenues. Polish-based customers of the company invested $40 million in advertising last year, Grey's president Edward Meyer said.

- The share stake of the Viscoplast band-aid maker addressed to large investors will most likely be taken over by an underwriting consortium led by the listed Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG), Viscoplast said.
PARKIET
- The National Investment Fund (NFI) Progress is conducting talks with prospective strategic investors for the Tymbark juice processing firm, the fund said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
